subject: biology
title: Land use and deforestation
key_idea: Humans take land for building, quarrying, farming and dumping waste, which removes habitats and reduces biodiversity. Destroying peat bogs and clearing tropical forest also adds carbon dioxide to the air, because decay and burning release it.

blocks.text: Humans reduce the land left for other animals and plants. This section covers how, and why it lowers biodiversity.

items.meaning: The variety of different species of plants, animals and microorganisms in an area.
The place where an organism lives.

items: **Building**, for example factories and houses.
**Quarrying** rocks.
**Farming**, for crops and livestock.
**Dumping waste**.
Habitats are lost, so the organisms that lived there die or move away.
Growing one crop (a monoculture) supports fewer species.
Hedgerows are removed to make fields larger.
Pesticides, insecticides and herbicides kill insects and plants, which damages food chains.
Fertiliser runs off into water and pollutes it.
Building, quarrying, farming and dumping waste reduce the land available to wildlife.
Loss of habitat reduces biodiversity.

blocks.text: Peat forms from the dead remains of plants in peat bogs. It is dug up for garden compost and to burn as fuel.

items: Peat bogs are a specialised habitat. Destroying them reduces the variety of plants, animals and microorganisms that live there.
Peat is a store of carbon, because it contains carbon compounds from dead plants.
When peat is dug up, oxygen enters it and microorganisms decay it quickly by aerobic respiration. This releases **carbon dioxide**.
Burning peat as fuel also releases carbon dioxide.
More carbon dioxide in the air increases global warming.

blocks.text: Gardeners and farmers want cheap peat compost to help produce more food. Conservationists want to protect peat bogs as habitats and to stop carbon dioxide being released.

items: Destroying peat bogs reduces biodiversity.
The decay or burning of peat releases carbon dioxide.
Cheap compost for food production conflicts with conserving peat bogs.

blocks.text: Deforestation is the clearing of large areas of forest. This section covers why it happens in tropical areas and what it does.

items: To provide land for **cattle** farming.
To provide land for **rice** fields.
To grow crops for **biofuels**.
Fewer trees take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
Burning waste wood releases carbon dioxide.
Microorganisms that decay the wood respire and release carbon dioxide.
More carbon dioxide leads to global warming.
Habitats are lost, so biodiversity falls.
Soil is eroded.

diagram.alt: Sort statements into reasons for tropical deforestation and effects of deforestation.
diagram.prompt: Sort each statement into a reason for deforestation or an effect of it.

items.text: Less carbon dioxide taken in by photosynthesis
Burning waste wood releases carbon dioxide
Decay by microorganisms releases carbon dioxide

items: Tropical forests are cleared for cattle, rice fields and biofuel crops.
Fewer trees and more burning and decay add carbon dioxide to the air.
Habitat loss reduces biodiversity.

checks.q: Name two ways humans reduce the land available for other animals and plants.
checks.a: Any two from: building, quarrying, farming, dumping waste.

checks.q: Explain why using peat for fuel is harmful to the environment.
checks.a: Burning peat releases carbon dioxide, which increases global warming.

checks.q: Give two reasons for large-scale deforestation in tropical areas, and one effect on the environment.
checks.a: Reasons: land for cattle and rice fields; to grow crops for biofuels. Effect: fewer trees so less carbon dioxide is taken in by photosynthesis, or loss of habitat reduces biodiversity.

worked_example.question:
Human activities affect the environment.

Describe the reasons why deforestation takes place and the effects deforestation has on the environment.
answer_points: Reasons: tropical rainforests are cleared for land to raise cattle, plant rice or plant crops such as coffee.
Land is also cleared for mining, or to grow biofuels or palm oil.
Temperate forests are cut down for wood for building or paper.
Effects: fewer trees take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
Decay by respiring microorganisms and burning waste wood release carbon dioxide.
The build-up of carbon dioxide causes the greenhouse effect and global warming.
Habitat loss reduces biodiversity, and soil erosion occurs.
worked_example.tip: Levelled answer. To reach the top level (4 to 6 marks) give both reasons and effects, in detail.

worked_example.question:
Deforestation is linked to an increase in global temperatures.

Explain how deforestation can contribute to an increase in global temperatures.
answer_points: Less photosynthesis, so less carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere.
Felled trees decompose, which adds carbon dioxide to the atmosphere.
Felled trees are burnt (combustion), which adds carbon dioxide to the atmosphere.
Carbon dioxide traps long wavelength (infrared) radiation from the ground.
worked_example.tip: Any three of these points score the marks.

blocks.text: Habitats are also destroyed by extracting natural resources and by pollution of fresh water and the sea.

items: **Extinction** of species that lose their habitat.
**Loss of soil**: with no roots to hold it, soil is washed away.
**Flooding**: with fewer trees to take up water, more rain runs off.
**Monoculture advantage:** one crop over a large area is easy to plant, treat and harvest, so yields are high and cost per crop is low.
**Monoculture disadvantage:** fewer habitats, so lower biodiversity. A pest or disease can spread quickly through the whole crop, and the crop takes the same nutrients from the soil each year.
(Supplement) **Conserving forests:** education about why forests matter, protected areas, quotas on the amount of timber cut, and replanting trees.

worked_example.question:
Loss of trees is known as deforestation.

Describe the effects of deforestation on an ecosystem.
answer_points: Reduces biodiversity, with loss of species and habitats.
Increases carbon dioxide, as less is absorbed because there is less photosynthesis.
Reduced soil quality, as fewer minerals are returned to the soil and minerals are leached.
Soil erosion, as soil is washed away.
Disturbs the water cycle: less transpiration and less rainfall.
worked_example.tip: Four different points score the four marks.

items: **Leaching**: minerals are washed out of the soil, so it becomes less fertile.
**Soil erosion**: with no roots to hold it, soil is washed away.
Less transpiration from the trees means less water vapour in the air, so less rainfall.
Less photosynthesis and more burning and decay change the carbon cycle and the balance of atmospheric gases: carbon dioxide rises.
